ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: 3 tablespoons, just enough to help the beans cook

steps.instruction: Wash the green beans, trim the ends, and cut into 2-3cm pieces.
Heat the coconut oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and let them crackle, then add the fennel and cumin seeds.
Add the shallots, garlic, and curry leaves. Sauté on low heat until the shallots turn soft and translucent, about 3-4 minutes.
Add the chopped tomato and cook for 1-2 minutes until it softens.
Add the green beans, water, salt, turmeric, chilli flakes (if using), and curry powder. Stir well to coat the beans.
Cover and cook over medium heat for about 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beans are just tender but still bright and slightly crisp.
Stir in the thick coconut milk and cook for a final minute, just enough to warm it through without overcooking the beans. Serve hot with rice.

source_site: kannammacooks.com, cross-checked against islandsmile.org for technique and ratio consistency

notes: This curry is sometimes called 'bonchi curry' generally, though the same method is also used for long beans (yardlong beans) -- a very similar, equally common Sri Lankan vegetable. Some households make a fully dry version with no coconut milk at all, finishing with just grated coconut instead (closer to a mallum style); this entry reflects the lightly creamy version more typical for everyday rice-and-curry meals. The dish should be cooked covered for the bean-tenderizing stage but only briefly once the coconut milk is added, to avoid losing the beans' bright colour and crisp-tender texture.
